flags.title: SNAP Work Requirements Rolled Out Statewide (Jan 2026)
flags.message: Oregon SNAP work requirements rolled out statewide January 2026. ABAWDs 18-54 must meet 80-hour/month work requirement. Exemptions: students, caregivers, people with disabilities, tribal members on reservations. Check county-specific waivers. Contact ODHS at 800-723-3638.

flags.title: Healthier Oregon Program — Undocumented Adults Covered
flags.message: Oregon covers undocumented adults 19-64 through the Healthier Oregon Program (OHP-like benefits). No immigration status barrier. Apply at ONE.Oregon.gov or call 800-699-9075. This is unique among US states.

flags.title: OR-EPRR Eviction Prevention — Active Court Case Required
flags.message: Oregon Emergency Rental Assistance (OR-EPRR) requires an active court case and monthly reapplication. Funds close quickly when available. Apply at OregonRentalAssistance.org. Also check local CAA programs and OHCS resources.

flags.title: SB 599 — Landlords Cannot Ask Immigration Status
flags.message: Oregon SB 599 (2025) prohibits landlords from asking about or discriminating based on immigration status. Violations reportable to BOLI (971-673-0761) and Fair Housing Council of Oregon (800-424-3247).

flags.title: Oregon Paid Family and Medical Leave (Advantage)
flags.message: Oregon Paid Leave provides 60-100% wage replacement for up to 12 weeks (14 for pregnancy complications). All workers who earned $1,000+ in base year qualify. Apply at paidleave.oregon.gov or call 833-854-0166.

flags.title: BOLI 6-Year Wage Claim SOL (Generous)
flags.message: Oregon allows wage claims going back 6 years under ORS 652.150 — among the most generous in the US. File with BOLI (971-673-0761). Also dual-file with federal DOL WHD for FLSA claims (2-3 year SOL).

flags.title: 7-Day Urgent Repair Timeline
flags.message: Oregon ORS 90.320 requires landlords to maintain habitable conditions. 7-day cure period for urgent repairs (30 days for non-urgent). Rent withhold (ORS 90.365) and repair-and-deduct available. Contact LASO CLEAR at 855-412-8429.

flags.title: 90-Day Retaliation Complaint Deadline
flags.message: Oregon retaliation complaints must be filed within 90 days under ORS 659A.199. If employer retaliates for wage claim or tenant exercises rights, file immediately with BOLI (971-673-0761).

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Oregon Emergency Hold
flags.message: OR involuntary psychiatric hold law: Oregon Emergency Hold. Statutory authority: ORS § 426.232. Maximum initial hold duration: 48 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 48 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in OR retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in OR: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Oregon Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Oregon Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
